Lowering phi0 from the best method should separate the nearly unretained first pair while retaining a similar gradient slope to assess the remaining close pair. The higher endpoint should elute the last compound promptly, targeting a complete run within 10 minutes.

Keep the best gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity at the sole unresolved pair. The other pairs have substantial resolution margins, and higher temperature should keep the final peak within 10 minutes.

An intermediate temperature should balance the two different close pairs seen at 45 and 60 C. A slightly shallower gradient adds separation while the observed retention times suggest the last peak should still elute within 10 minutes.
Injection 11 achieved the maximum possible CRF; retain it as the benchmark. Shorten only tG by one grid step to test whether full resolution can be maintained with faster elution.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope to recover resolution of the R=1.38 pair while preserving the eight-minute gradient. This intermediate slope between injections 11 and 12 should keep the last peak below 10 minutes and may restore CRF 1.000 with faster elution than injection 11.

Lowering the starting organic fraction should improve the middle pair that lost resolution when phi0 increased. The steeper overall gradient may offset the added initial retention, offering a faster fully resolved method than injection 13.

Test a cooler selectivity regime to move the middle co-elution seen at 45 C in the opposite direction from the 55 C optimum. This may provide larger critical-pair margins for subsequent gradient compression; injection 15 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction at 60 C moves the middle pair beyond its co-elution point, opening a faster selectivity window. This is exploratory: monitor the first pair for excessive compression while retaining injection 15 as the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Lower phi0 to recover the first-pair resolution lost in injection 17, while steepening the gradient to test separation on the reversed-order side of the middle-pair crossing. This targets a faster fully resolved run, with particular attention to the neighboring middle pairs.

Shorten only tG to test whether further steepening separates the remaining middle pair on this fast, reversed-order branch. Monitor its neighboring pair, currently at R=1.62, for loss of resolution; injection 15 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Test an intermediate-temperature, higher-starting-organic window to balance the two critical middle pairs while shortening retention. Cooling from 60 to 50 C should also improve the early-pair separation that limited injection 17; injection 15 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Lengthen injection 14’s gradient by one step to recover its sole unresolved pair while retaining the higher starting organic fraction. This tests another potentially fully resolved method below 10 minutes; injection 15 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.
